answer: In the Reproducibility Project: Psychology (project == 'rpp'), 16 of the 35 successfully replicated studies (45.7%) have a junior professor (Assistants or Assistant Professors) as the most senior replication author (seniority.r); the remaining categories are Professor (8), Associate Professor (7), and Researcher (4). Caveats for unambiguous reading: the proportion would be 57.1% (20/35) if 'Researcher' is counted as junior, and 0% if the original study's authors (seniority.o) rather than the replication authors are used — the intended reading is the 45.7% replication-author figure. File 2 (replication_success CSV) is excluded from the computation because it lacks seniority and `replicated` columns and shares no rows with File 1's rpp studies; only File 1 was used.

payload.workflow: Loaded File 1 only (File 2 excluded by design). Filtered to project=='rpp' (97 studies), then to replicated==1 (35 studies). Sanity-checked uniqueness (97/97 unique ids; 35/35 unique ids, no duplicate rows). Tabulated seniority.r among the 35 replicated studies; counted 'Assistant' + 'Assistant Professor' = 16 -> 16/35 = 45.7%. Computed sensitivity variants (incl Researcher 57.1%; no replication filter 39.2%; seniority.o 0%) for unambiguous reporting.
payload.hypothesis: In the Reproducibility Project: Psychology (project=='rpp'), 16 of 35 successfully replicated studies (45.7%) have a junior professor (Assistant or Assistant Professor) as the most senior replication author.
